title: Can AI Solve the Peer Review Crisis? A Large-Scale, Cross-Model Experiment of LLMs’ Performance and Biases in Evaluating over 1,000 Economics Papers

bias_targets.methodology: Systematically varying author names on economics papers to represent male versus female identities (both prominent and randomly generated) and comparing the LLM-assigned quality ratings to a fully anonymized baseline.

Assigning different institutional affiliations (e.g., MIT, Harvard, LSE, University of Cape Town, Chulalongkorn University) to the authors of papers and measuring the impact on the LLMs' publication recommendation scores.
Replacing the original authors of papers with either top-ranked, famous economists or randomly generated non-academic names to evaluate if LLMs exhibit favoritism toward well-known scholars.
